title: Geometric Cumulative and Tail Probabilities, Intervals, and Thresholds

questions.title: Geometric Tail Probability More Than r Trials

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with success probability $p = 0.20$. Find $P(X > 5)$, giving your answer as an exact decimal.

questions.title: Cumulative Geometric Probability No More Than r Trials

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with success probability $p = 0.15$. Find $P(X \le 4)$, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: At Least r Trials Boundary Translation

parts.text: A fair six-sided die is rolled repeatedly until a 6 appears. Let $X$ be the number of rolls required. Find $P(X \ge 4)$, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.

questions.title: Geometric Interval Probability via Cumulative Subtraction

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with parameter $p = 0.30$. Find $P(3 \le X \le 6)$, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: Logarithmic Solution for Sample Size Threshold

parts.text: An experiment has success probability $p = 0.25$ on each independent trial. Find the least number of trials $n$ required such that the probability of obtaining at least one success is greater than $0.90$.

questions.title: Recovering Parameter from a Tail Probability

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution such that $P(X > 3) = 0.216$. Find the value of $p$, and calculate $P(X \le 2)$.

questions.title: Ratio-Defined Confectionery: Tail and Cumulative Probabilities

parts.text: A candy machine dispenses sweets in flavours mint, orange, and berry in the ratio $3 : 4 : 5$. Sweets are dispensed independently until the first mint sweet appears. Let $X$ be the number of sweets dispensed. Find $P(X > 6)$, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form and as a decimal correct to 4 significant figures.
Find the probability that no more than 4 sweets are dispensed, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.

questions.title: Customer Shopping Mode: Early Success and Sample Size Threshold

parts.text: A retail survey indicates that each customer shops online with probability $0.32$, independently of other customers. Customers are interviewed one by one until the first customer who shops online is found. Find the probability that the first customer who shops online is among the first 3 customers interviewed, giving your answer as an exact decimal.
Find the least number of customers $n$ that must be interviewed so that the probability that at least one customer shops online is greater than $0.96$.

questions.title: Dice Outcomes: Bounded Interval and Stringent Target Threshold

parts.text: A fair six-sided die is rolled repeatedly until either a 1 or a 6 is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of rolls required. Find $P(3 \le X \le 6)$, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.
Find the least number of throws $n$ such that the probability of obtaining at least one 1 or 6 in $n$ throws is greater than $0.995$.

questions.title: Industrial Component Screening: Interval and Carton Sizing

parts.text: A manufacturing process produces light bulbs where each bulb has a probability of $0.06$ of being defective, independently of all other bulbs. Bulbs are tested one by one until the first defective bulb is found. Let $X$ be the number of bulbs tested. Find $P(5 \le X \le 12)$, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.
Bulbs are packed into cartons of size $N$. Find the smallest carton size $N$ such that the probability that a carton contains at least one defective bulb is at least $0.80$.

questions.title: Parameter Recovery from Tail Probability to Half-Open Interval

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with parameter $p$. Given that $P(X > 4) = 0.2401$, find the exact value of $p$.
Using $p = 0.30$, find $P(2 \le X < 5)$, giving your answer as an exact decimal.

questions.title: Target Archery: Tail Probability, Threshold, and Multi-Archer Round

parts.text: An archer hits the target with probability $0.22$ on any independent shot. Shots are taken until the target is hit. Let $X$ be the number of shots required. Find $P(X > 5)$, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.
Find the least number of shots $n$ such that the probability that the archer hits the target at least once exceeds $0.95$.

Four archers, each having independent success probability $0.22$ per shot, shoot simultaneously. In each round, all four archers shoot once. Let $Y$ be the number of rounds until at least one archer hits the target. Find $P(Y \le 2)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Industrial Stress Testing: Interval, Batch Sizing, and Batch Acceptance

parts.text: A sensitive electronic component fails a severe stress test with probability $0.12$, independently of other components. Components are tested one by one until the first component fails. Let $X$ be the number of components tested. Find $P(4 \le X \le 10)$, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.
Components are tested in batches of size $k$. Find the least value of $k$ such that the probability that a batch of $k$ components contains at least one failure is greater than $0.75$.

Five independent batches, each containing 11 components, are tested. Find the probability that exactly 4 of the 5 batches contain at least one failure, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
